_comment: Plugin manifest (authored by the plugin author). 'version' is the plugin semver (release-only); install-plugin reads 'setup'.
name: resource-sharing
description: Share hosts between agents and projects with claim files kept on each host (~/.solaris/claims/). tools/hostclaims.py (stdlib Python 3.8+, run on the controller, sent to each host over ssh as `python3 -`; no daemon, no central server, no root) claims cores, GPUs by index with a time-slicing share (P0 1.0, P1 0.5, P2/P3 0.25) and memory, RAM and disk under a flock so checking capacity and writing a claim are one step; counts a claim's memory as PSS, never grants cores a running job is pinned to, ties claims to their jobs' processes (repeat claim --pid), renews claims in place (renew), yields paired claims in a set order (--yield-with); counts unclaimed GPU processes, memory, RAM and CPU load as used and tags each host free, partly-busy or busy; launches jobs in tmux pinned with taskset and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, with a heartbeat, a done marker with the exit code, and release on exit; moves stale claims (old heartbeat and no process, or a changed boot id) to stale/ and keeps orphans; delivers yield requests to preemptible lower-priority jobs older than 20 minutes (TERM, then KILL after a grace); reports GPU-hours and CPU-hours per project; and keeps named shared counters with per-project caps for account-level limits. Projects in one Solaris tree share hosts through sharing links (resource-sharing.json: project slug and share_with), discovered automatically (a host is private to its owner until its list names others); guests see new, gone and changed shared hosts with `shared` (a seen list, no ssh; exit 6 until acknowledged) and owners share new machines at once with `install --all`; every host has exactly one owner, acting only as its own project, who alone installs, renews, extends, maintains, releases or deletes it, while guests file (and may withdraw) extension, maintenance and release-objection requests the owner approves or declines. Lease kinds none, free and paid (paid cloud instances such as Brev: planned end, $/h, GPU type, instance); a fit command ranks existing hosts against launching a new instance (its wait and its dollars) and recommends reuse, reuse with an extension request, or launch new; an owner audit lists lease end, idle time, work outside claims, use by project, cost so far, open requests and a keep/extend/decline/release/delete/check recommendation, with a stricter idle limit for paid hosts and never a delete or release under running work. The skill covers setup, commands, priorities, ownership, picking up shared hosts, fit, audit and pools; the always-on rule keeps jobs inside their claims, other projects' claims untouched, host changes with the owner, what guests write on a host (caches included) inside their own folder there, sharing changes picked up (guests run `shared` at least hourly and act on new and gone hosts before acknowledging; owners run `install --all` after adding machines or changing share_with), shared hosts from being deleted or stopped without the audit's advice (guarding other plugins' teardowns), and paid instances from being extended on one's own or left idle. Beside it, tools/hosthealth.py checks GPU hosts over the same inventory (GPUs against the inventory, Xid codes, GPU start failures, throttling, ECC, persistence, MIG and compute modes, power limits, CPU governor) and with --fix applies the safe performance settings (persistence mode, the GPU power limit at its default, or at the most each GPU allows with --power max on owned hosts, performance governor) on owned hosts or on what the caller's live claims hold; tools/hostdash.py shows each host's load, GPU use, claims, tmux sessions and busiest processes live over one reused ssh connection per host.

optional.name: nvidia-brev
optional.why: launch a paid instance when fit says launch-new

notes: List the project's hosts in <pack>/.memory/hosts.json (<pack> is the project's ai-pack folder: default aipack/, ai/ in older projects, any name) as [{name, target, opts}] (target user@address, opts the ssh options), with an optional owner (project slug) and lease ({kind: none|free|paid, planned_end, usd_per_hour, gpu_type, instance}).

To share hosts with other projects in this Solaris tree, create <pack>/.memory/resource-sharing.json: {"project": "<slug>", "share_with": ["<other-slug>"]} (an optional policy block holds weights, class defaults, fit and audit thresholds). Hosts that other projects share with this one are merged in automatically. Without the file, this project's hosts stay private to it.

Install every host this project owns with `python3 <pack>/plugins/resource-sharing/tools/hostclaims.py install --all` from the project root (again right after adding machines or changing share_with, then tell the projects you share with; hosts need Python 3.8+, tmux and taskset), and record the footprint ~/.solaris/claims/ on each host in <pack>/.memory/resources.md. Owners run `audit` at least every two hours (hourly for paid hosts) and delete or release a shared host only on its advice. Guests run `hostclaims.py shared` at every audit and at least hourly: it lists new, gone and changed hosts shared with the project (exit 6 until `shared --ack`).
